newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: INTERVIEW-Daewoo Motor raises export forecast.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Daewoo Motor raises export forecast.

text.p: Daewoo Motor Co, a unit of South Korea's Daewoo Group, has raised its export forecast to 430,000 units in calendar 1997 from an earlier projection of 400,000, the company chairman said on Thursday.
Chairman Kim Tae-gou said three new passenger car models introduced since last November and the strong yen would help increase Daewoo's car exports.
"Dealers overseas have responded positively to our new models ... (which) are competitive both quality-wise and price-wise," Kim said in an interview.
Daewoo's finished car exports totalled 352,900 units last year.

He added that South Korea's struggling auto industry was expected to rebound near the end of this year in line with an economic recovery. The strength of the yen against the dollar would help boost Korean car exports, he said.
A stronger Japanese currency tends to make Korea's won-based exports relatively cheaper.
"Fears of excess capacity seem to be somewhat exaggerated by carmakers in advanced nations," Kim said.

He said a carmaker must have an annual capacity of at least two million units to reach economy of scale. Daewoo's current capacity is 1.6 million units, which is scheduled to rise to 2.5 million by 2000.
Kim said the expected business recovery would help Daewoo meet this year's sales and profit targets.
"I'm confident we will post a net profit of 80 billion won this year on sales of about 6.8 trillion won," Kim said.
The projections compare with slightly more than 50 billion won net profit on a turnover of 4.3 trillion won last year.
But he said Daewoo's domestic vehicle sales would fall to 450,000 units from an earlier projection of 480,000 because of a slump in earlier this year.

He said new sub-compact Lanos and compact Nubira and Leganza models would help Daewoo Motor increase its local market share to about 35 percent this year from last year's 25 percent and further to 40 percent in 1998.
"I think local car sales will pick up in the second half of this year in line with a recovery in the economy," he added.
Kim said his company would ship more than 20,000 cars to the United States in the fourth quarter of this year to resume marketing there.
Daewoo agreed to stay out of the U.S. as part of an agreement ending its 15-year partnership with General Motors Corp in 1992.
Kim put Daewoo's U.S. sales at 50,000 cars next year and between 100,000 and 150,000 in 2000.
Commenting on the need to restructure the nation's crowded auto industry, Kim said the issue was not a pressing matter.
"We may have to wait two to three years before we can judge whether the industry needs restructuring," he said.
Kim added Samsung Motors Inc of the Samsung Group SAGR.CN must resolve the continuing turmoil in the local industry caused by its internal report criticising Kia Motors Corp's management.
"Samsung's mention of another company's managerial matters is morally inappropriate," he said.

Analysts said Samsung was measuring public opinion about its takeover of Kia when it proposed in an internal report, widely believed to have been intentionally leaked to the media, to restructure the crowded domestic auto industry.
